title: Which Lands First? Projectiles Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Aarav flicks one coin off his study table and drops another at the same moment. The flicked coin flies far, the other falls straight down. Which hits the floor first? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we find out, and learn exactly why every throw makes the same curve: one throw is two motions, steady across and free fall up and down.

On a live motion notebook a dropped ball and a pushed ball fall side by side with strobe flashes, a height graph and a slow-mo replay of their velocity vectors. Then a 20 m/s throw at 30 degrees is split into u cos theta and u sin theta, and we derive x = (u cos theta) t, y = (u sin theta) t - 1/2 g t^2, vx and vy step by step (g = 9.8 m/s^2). Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example, the exam trap about acceleration at the highest point, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Two coins: which lands first?
0:28 What is a projectile?
0:49 Motion notebook: drop vs push
1:45 An angled throw, split in two
2:18 The rules: x, y, vx and vy step by step
3:00 Side by side + pause and think
3:31 Worked example: a ball at 1.5 s
4:17 Exam trap: acceleration at the top
4:40 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:27 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Trajectory of a Projectile. Why does every throw make the very same curve?
